title: Testing the Unknown: A Framework for OpenMP Testing via Random Program Generation
problem: OpenMP compiler implementations (GCC, Clang, Intel) contain performance anomalies and correctness issues that are difficult to expose using manual test creation. Current verification relies on manually crafted tests with limited coverage of possible program behaviors.
motivation: OpenMP is fundamental to parallel and HPC computing, so ensuring correctness and performance consistency across different compiler implementations is critical for application portability and reliability.
method: The framework automatically generates random but structurally valid OpenMP programs using a grammar (a set of rules defining legal program structures), building on the Varity program generator. These generated tests run against three OpenMP compiler implementations (GCC, Clang, Intel) in parallel, comparing their outputs—a technique called differential testing—to identify cases where they disagree or produce incorrect results. Across 1,800 generated tests, the researchers found patterns indicating which types of programs most reliably expose compiler bugs.
key_novelty: Use grammar-based random program generation to automatically create diverse OpenMP tests for differential compiler validation, instead of writing tests manually.
contributions: A randomized differential testing framework for OpenMP compiler implementations
Grammar-based random program generation extension for OpenMP in the Varity tool
Discovery of multiple performance anomalies and correctness bugs in GCC, Clang, and Intel OpenMP
Classification and analysis of test categories exposing compiler implementation issues
primary_theme: Automated OpenMP compiler testing via random program generation
